Briefly stated the case of the prosecution is that on the intervening night of 14.05.2014-15.05.2014, the accused Jai Prakash approached the immigration counter seeking State vs Jai Prakash on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133131935/
1 departure clearance to Damam. During scrutiny of his travel documents, it was found that the POE sticker No. 220353 dated 09.09.2010 affixed on page No. 30 of his passport was suspected to be fake.

The passport was sent to Protector of Emigrants-II, Govt. of India, Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs, Mumbai for verification and after verification, it was found that the said POE sticker was found to be fake.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the present FIR was registered on the complaint of immigration.

During the course of investigation, the accused disclosed that he obtained the POE sticker from a company Spicejet Engineering Construction in Mumbai in lieu of Rs. 40,000/- in the year 2010 but this company was fake and has cheated many persons.
He further disclosed that he has travelled abroad in 2012 and 2014 also but he has not used the POE sticker as the same was not genuine.
The details of the company was not with the accused and hence, the investigation could not be proceeded against the company.
After conclusion of the investigation, the charge sheet was filed against the accused under section 474 IPC & 12 PP Act.
2. Upon filing of the present chargesheet, cognizance of the offence was taken, accused was summoned and compliance with Sec. 207 Cr.P.C was ensured.

Vide order dated 31.08.2018, charge under section 474 IPC, section 417 read with section 511 IPC and section 12 Passport Act was framed against the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Thereafter, the case was fixed for recording of the prosecution evidence.
3. The prosecution has examined as many as seven witnesses.

Prosecution examined Sh. Raj Sahil,
JIO-II as PW1, who deposed that on the intervening night of 14.05.2014 and 15.05.2014, he was performing his duty as CO at counter No. 32 with stamp No. 336 in Departure Wing of Immigration,
IGI Airport, New Delhi.

That during the clearance of Flight No. Air India 913, one passenger namely Jai Prakash was holding Indian Passport, the number of which he did not remember issued from Lucknow, approached his counter for immigration clearance to Damam.
That on scrutiny of his passport, it was found that the POE sticker No. 220353 dated 09.09.2010 affixed on page No. 30 of his passport seems to be fake.
That thereafter, he seized his passport vide seizure memo Ex.PW1/A and sent it to Mumbai for verification.
That on 21.08.2014, he received the verification report Ex.P1 in respect to the said passport and as per the report, the said POE sticker No. 220353 was not genuine.
That thereafter, he prepared the complaint/rukka Ex.PW1/B and handed over the same to the duty officer for registration of FIR.
That the duty officer seized the passport and copy of the passport, verification of POE sticker vide seizure memo Ex.PW1/C.
The witness correctly identified the accused, passport Ex.P2 and the POE sticker Ex.P3.

The witness was cross-examined by Ld.
Counsel for the accused.
4. The prosecution examined Sh. Raj Kumar, ACIO-I as PW2, who appeared on behalf of Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, Asstt. Director, Central Foreigners Bureau (CFB).
The witness produced a sealed envelope in the name of the Court with the seal of CFB/MS.

Upon opening the envelope, it was found containing an authority letter Ex.PW2/A issued to the name of the witness and certificate U/s. 65B of Indian Evidence Act Ex.PW2/B, issued by Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, Asstt. Director,
Central Foreigners Bureau (CFB).

The envelope also contained certified record the arrival and departure record Ex. PW2/C in respect to Mr. Jai Prakash bearing the signatures of Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, Asstt. Director, Central Foreigners Bureau (CFB), New Delhi on all pages.
The witness was cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused.

The prosecution examined ASI Bachchu Ram as PW3, who deposed that on 21.08.14, he was posted at PS IGI Airport as Head Constable and was posted as Duty Officer.

That on that day, Ct.
Pradeep brought rukka for registration of FIR.

That he made endorsement on the rukka Ex.PW3/A.
That he has registered the FIR Ex.PW3/B (OSR).
That he handed over the copy of FIR and original rukka to SI Harkesh for further investigation.
The witness was not cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused despite opportunity being given in this regard.
6. The prosecution examined Sh. Sushil Kumar, Under Secretary, MHA as PW4, who deposed that on 12.08.2014, he was working as POE-II, in the office of Protector of Emmigrants, Mumbai.

That on that day, passport No. G3401025 dated 04.06.2014 issued from Lucknow to verify POE sticker,
was received in the office.

That after going through the office record, it was found that sticker No.
220353 dated 09.09.2010 affixed on the said passport belonging to the accused Jai Prakash was not genuine and same was not issued from their office.
That he has given his report dated 12.08.2014 Ex.PW4/A.
The witness was not cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused despite opportunity being given in this regard.
7. The prosecution examined Inspector Vishram Meena as PW5, who deposed that on 02.07.2015,
he was posted at PS IGI Airport as Sub-Inspector.
That he received the case file from MHCR for further investigation in the present matter.
That after receiving the file, he served notice under Section 41 Cr.PC to accused and he joined the investigation.
That after discussing with the senior police officials, he found that evidence under Section 420/468/471 IPC are not found against the accused sections 474 IPC and 12 PP Act were added.
That thereafter, he formally arrested the accused vide arrest memo Ex.PW5/A.
That he recorded the disclosure statement of the accused Ex.PW5/B.
That he obtained the ID of the accused Mark-I (colly) and filed the same after taking the photocopy of the same.
That accused was released on police bail after furnishing bail bond Ex.PW5/C.

That thereafter, he sent a letter to Emmigration department, Ministry of Home Affairs,
Govt. of India for seeking arrival and departure in respect of accused.
That on 23.05.2016, he received a letter from the said Ministry with the details of accused showing his arrival and departure entries Ex.PW5/D (colly).
That he also got verified the passport of the accused from the Ministry of External Affairs and as per the report Ex.PW5/E, the same was found genuine.
That he recorded the statement of Ct. Biney Kumar under Section 161 Cr.PC but in the meanwhile, he was transferred and handed over the case file to the MHCR.
The witness correctly identified the accused.
The witness was cross- examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused.

8. The prosecution examined Inspector Harkesh Gaba as PW6, who deposed that on on 21.08.2014,
he was posted as Sub-Inspector at PS IGI Airport.
That on that day, DO PS IGI Airport handed over him original rukka, copy of FIR No.291/14, seizure memo along with seized documents.
That thereafter, he examined all the witnesses and their statements were recorded U/s.161 Cr.PC.
That thereafter, in January, 2015, he got transferred from PS IGI Airport to Outer District and handed over the case file to the MHC(R) of PS IGI Airport.
The witness was cross-
examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused.

3 9.
The prosecution examined Inspector Vipin Kumar as PW7, who deposed that in August 2017, he was posted as Sub- Inspector at PS IGI Airport.
That the further investigation of the present case was marked to him.
That thereafter, he collected the file from MHCR and gone through the same.
That since investigation in the present case was already completed, therefore, he filed the charge-sheet in the present case.
The witness was cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused.

10. After, completion of the prosecution on 22.03.2024, the prosecution evidence was closed and the case was fixed for recording of the statement of accused under section 313 Cr.P.C.
11.
The statement of the accused under section 313 Cr.P.C was recorded on 28.11.2024.
The accused stated that he was falsely implicated in the present case by the complainant and the IO.
He stated that he was a victim in the present case as he was cheated by someone.
12. The accused led defence evidence.
The accused examined himself as DW1 and deposed that he had handed over his passport to Spic Jelen Company asheI had to go Aman.
That the company took around 40,000/- for arranging Visa for Aman.
That he also handed over all documents to the company for arranging Visa.
That he also participated in the interview.
That he was called to Puna where the company handed over to him his passport and ticket.
That thereafter, he went to Mumbai Airport where the staff of the Airport informed that his ticket was fake.
That he was detained at Airport as the visa and ticket was fake.
The accused cross-examined by Ld. APP for the State.
13. I have heard the arguments from Ld. APP for the State and Ld. LAC for the accused.
14. In a criminal trial, the onus remains on the prosecution to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts and benefit of doubt, if any, must necessarily go in favour of the accused.
It is for the prosecution to travel the entire distance from may have to must have.
If the prosecution appears to be improbable or lacks credibility the benefit of doubt necessarily has to go to the accused.

In this regard, it is relevant to reproduce the observations made by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kali Ram Vs.
Himanchal Pradesh (1973 2 SCC 808) in para 23 and 25 which are reproduced as under:
" 23.

Himanchal Pradesh (1973 2 SCC 808)

sentences.text:
Observations in a recent decision of this Court, Shivaji Sahabrao Bobade & Anr.
v. State of Maharashtra (1973 2 SCC 793) to which reference has been made during arguments were not intended to make a departure from the rule of the presumption of innocence of the accused and his entitlement to the benefit of reasonable doubt in criminal cases.

entities.text:
Shivaji Sahabrao Bobade & Anr.
v. State of Maharashtra (1973 2 SCC 793)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: One of the cardinal principles which has always to be kept in view in our system of administration of justice for criminal cases is that a person arraigned as an accused is presumed to be innocent unless that presumption is rebutted by the prosecution by production of evidence as may show him to be guilty of the offence with which he is charged.
The burden of proving the guilt of the accused is upon the prosecution and unless it relieves itself of that burden, the courts cannot record a finding of the guilt of the accused.

There are certain cases in which statutory presumptions arise regarding the guilt of the accused, but the burden even in those cases is upon the prosecution to prove the existence of facts which have to be present before the presumption can be drawn.

Once those facts are shown by the prosecution State vs Jai Prakash on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133131935/
4 to exist, the court can raise the statutory presumption and it would, in such an event,
be for the accused to rebut the presumption.
The onus even in such cases upon the accused is not as heavy as is normally upon the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused.

If some material is brought on the record consistent with the innocence of the accused which may reasonably be true, even though it is not positively proved to be true, the accused would be entitled to acquittal.

Leaving aside the cases of statutory presumptions, the onus is upon the prosecution to prove the different ingredients of the offence and unless it discharges that onus, the prosecution cannot succeed...
xxxxxx 25.

Another golden thread which runs through the web of the administration of justice in criminal cases is that if two views are possible on the evidence adduced in the case, one pointing to the guilt of the accused and the other to his innocence, the view which is favourable to the accused should be adopted.
This principle has a special relevance in cases wherein the guilt of the accused is sought to be established by circumstantial evidence.

Rule has accordingly been laid down that unless the evidence adduced in the case is consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused and is inconsistent with that of his innocence, the court should refrain from recording a finding of guilt of the accused.
It is also an accepted rule that in case the 73 5 court entertains reasonable doubt regarding the, guilt of the accused, the accused must have the benefit of that doubt.

Of course, the doubt regarding the guilt of the accused should be reasonable : it is not the doubt of a mind which is either so vacillating that it is incapable of reaching a firm conclusion or so timid that it is hesitant and afraid to take things to their natural consequences.
The rule regarding the benefit of doubt also does not warrant acquittal of the accused by resort to surmises, conjectures or fanciful considerations.

As mentioned by us recently in the case of State of Punjab v. Jagir Singh,(1974 2 SCC 227) a criminal trial is not like a fairy tale wherein one is free to give flight to one's imagination and fantasy.

entities.text: State of Punjab v. Jagir Singh,(1974 2 SCC 227)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It concerns itself with the question as to whether the accused arraigned at the trial is guilty of the offence with which he is charged.
Crime is an event in real life and is the product of interplay of different human emotions.

In arriving at the conclusion about the guilt of the accused charged with the commission of a crime, the, court has to judge, the evidence by the yardstick of probabilities, its intrinsic worth and the animus of witnesses.
Every case in the final analysis would have to depend upon its own facts.

Although the benefit of every reasonable doubt should be given to the accused, the courts should not at the same time reject evidence which is ex facie trustworthy, on grounds which are fanciful or in the nature of conjectures."
15. In the present case, the chain of proper custody of the case property i.e. passport was not proved.
The PW1/Complainant deposed that he handed over the complaint to the duty officer alongwith the passport and that the duty officer has seized the passport vide seizure memo Ex.PW1/C.

When PW3 was duty officer called for his examination, he deposed that the rukka was brought to him by one Ct.

5
Pradeep and after registration of FIR, he handed over the FIR for investigation to PW 6 SI Harkesh.
He has not deposed anything about the seizure memo.
Further, his testimony is in stark contrast to the testimony of PW1.
There is contradiction as to who brought the rukka to the police station and how the seizure of the passport was prepared.
Since, the proper chain of custody of the case property has not been proved, the benefit of the same shall go to the accused.

16. In view of the above discussion, the prosecution has been able to prove its case against the accused accused Jai Prakash for the charge under section 474 IPC, 417 r/w 511 IPC and Section 12 PP Act beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, the accused Jai Prakash is acquitted of the offences under section 474 IPC, 417 r/w 511 IPC and Section 12 PP Act.
